DCF interview question

The cash flow question that trips up juniors.

One question. 20 seconds.

Unlevered free cash flow

EBIT $100. Tax 25%. D&A $20. Capex $30. NWC up $10. UFCF?

A$65
B$55
C$45
D$75

Lock it in, then swipe.

Answer
$55
$75
EBIT after tax: $100 × 75%
+$20
Add back D&A (not cash)
−$40
Capex $30 + NWC $10

B. 75 + 20 − 30 − 10 = 55

Why no interest?

Unlevered means before debt.

It's the cash the business makes for everyone who funded it, lenders and shareholders. So interest stays out.

Most common miss

NWC went up, so cash goes down.

More inventory or receivables ties up cash. People add it and get $75.

What did you pick? 👇

Red flag or green flag?

4 answers to "Why banking?"

Judge each one before you swipe.

Answer 1

"Honestly? The money."

🚩

Everyone knows it pays. Saying only that tells them nothing about why you'd last 100-hour weeks.

Answer 2

"I built a DCF for my club's stock pitch and want to do that on live deals."

🟢

Specific, real, and it shows you've already done the work.

Answer 3

"I just want to keep my options open."

🚩

Sounds like you'll leave in a year. Talk about what you want to learn instead.

Answer 4

"I talked to analysts on your team and liked how much they own their deals."

🟢

Only if it's true. Which one would you say? 👇
